_meta.description: Core reference tables for the Lal Kitab system: permanent houses (pakka ghar), planetary friendships/enemies as used in Lal Kitab, significations, and the rules that decide whether a planet is benefic or malefic in a chart. Variants exist across Lal Kitab editions (1939/1941/1942/1952); values here follow the most commonly cited tradition.
_meta.disclaimer: Lal Kitab remedies are traditional and cultural. They are not a substitute for medical, legal, financial or psychological advice. Surface this disclaimer with every remedy shown to a user.

pakka_ghar._note: Permanent / fixed house of each planet. A planet in its pakka ghar is strong and well-placed; the lord of a pakka ghar acts as a substitute when the planet sits elsewhere.

friendship._note: Lal Kitab broadly follows natural (naisargik) friendships. F=friend, E=enemy, N=neutral.

planet_states._note: Lal Kitab classifies a planet's condition. These drive whether a remedy is needed.
planet_states.sleeping: Planet that gives no result until 'awakened'; often when alone with no aspect/conjunction.
planet_states.awakened: Active planet giving full results (good or bad).
planet_states.blind: Planet that misfires its results onto the wrong house/person.
planet_states.benefic: Planet placed in a friendly house or with friends; gives supportive results.
planet_states.malefic: Planet in an enemy house or with enemies; the case where remedies are prescribed.

malefic_conditions._note: Heuristics this engine uses to flag a planet as malefic (needing a remedy). Any one may apply.
rules: Planet sits in the house of an enemy planet's pakka ghar.
Planet is conjunct an enemy planet.
Sun + Saturn together, Sun + Rahu (grahan), or Moon + Rahu/Ketu (grahan).
Planet debilitated or in the 8th/12th with no friendly support.
A 'blind' or 'sleeping' planet relevant to the user's stated problem.
